title: How to Leverage Domain Expertise — Chris Lovejoy, Notius Labs
talk_summary: Chris Lovejoy argues that vertical AI success is an organizational problem, not a model problem, and presents a framework where domain experts act as oracle (directly tweak prompts/outputs), evaluator (define metrics and review systems), or architect (design self-improving loops). He illustrates with Granola, Tandem, and Anterior case studies showing how the role evolves with scale and measurability.

takeaways.technique: Principal domain expert as single accountable quality owner
takeaways.what_they_do: Designate one individual ultimately accountable for AI output quality who can make decisions, avoiding consensus-by-committee and giving them time to deeply study failure modes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a single individual who's ultimately accountable for the quality of the AI performance and makes can therefore like make decisions

takeaways.technique: Evaluator role: define metrics and build a review dashboard
takeaways.what_they_do: Domain expert defines objective metrics and failure modes, then builds a dashboard so reviewers can sample outputs and feed structured data back to engineers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I then defined metrics and failure modes. Um I built a review dashboard to enable clinicians to come in and look at certain outputs

takeaways.technique: Decentralized oracle: many specialists owning sub-segments
takeaways.what_they_do: When one expert can't cover all variation, split ownership across many domain experts each owning a subset (specialty, region, use case) with per-subset prompt versions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they went the approach of a decentralized oracle and hired out um various other doctors to um basically do this in kind of like subsets

takeaways.technique: Evolve the expert role as scale changes (oracle→evaluator→architect)
takeaways.what_they_do: Start a domain expert as an oracle doing manual iteration; when manual iteration is too slow and metrics exist, move them to evaluator then architect of automated improvement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if manual iteration is too slow, and you can identify methods to automate improvements, then you might uh progress to a kind of an architect model

takeaways.technique: Hire for breadth beyond raw domain expertise
takeaways.what_they_do: Pick people with domain expertise as the base plus adjacent skills (prompting, data-science intuition, engineering) so they can grow across oracle/evaluator/architect roles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hiring somebody who has the domain expertise kind of is is the base and needs to be a given. But then as many of those skills as possible
